evidence_quotes.name_asked_and_used: Joanna: 'May I have your email address, please?' and later uses 'William' multiple times throughout the call.
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'It might take about ten to fifteen minutes, if it's a good time.' — time-boxed but no explicit promise of dependable quote or clear wait for yes before continuing.
evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Joanna: 'As we speak with customers everyday, they do have concerns about their moves like damages to their items, movers not arriving on time. Are there any of your concerns as well?' — asked before any logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concerns (items not getting damaged, movers arriving on time, everything 'on the up and up'). Joanna responds with 'Of course, I can' and 'Yes sir' and 'Mm-hmm' acknowledgments but does not probe deeper with 'tell me more about that' or follow-up silence to explore the concerns further.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Joanna: 'Of course. Thank you so much. I agree.' — acknowledges but does not reflect back a summary of what was heard in structured form.
evidence_quotes.promises_delivered: Joanna: 'Now for every move we also include our no worries damage coverage which would give you guys up to $2,000 coverage for any accidental damages, also meet your mover feature. Rest assured we don't take, I can track the workers. And lastly on time guarantee if we run late, we provide discounts for your move.' — both On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage mentioned with terms.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent question asked after delivering the promises.
evidence_quotes.concern_led_opening: Joanna: 'What items in this move are you most concerned about?' — asked and opened the probing step concern-led.
evidence_quotes.logistics_gathered: Addresses (valley forge drive to piping rock lane), property types (one story to two story), square footage (2200), bedrooms (4), garage items (gym equipment, squat rack, rower, bumper plates), special items (wall-mounted TVs, small gun safe, glass-top tables, office desk), walking distances discussed implicitly through the TV discussion.
evidence_quotes.packing_asked: Joanna: 'And are you also planning to get help with packing your stuff into boxes?' — asked.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Joanna: 'Typically for a house this, we might end up with about a 115 to a 135 boxes once everything's already packed. Do you think you would just fall within that range?' — asked with typical range provided.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Joanna: 'typically for, if you're planning to do a move on a Tuesday this is actually one of our lowest hourly rate for the week, which is $95 per hour per mover' — Customer is already on Tuesday (a Best Value Day per the context). No flexibility question about switching to a cheaper day is appropriate or asked.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: The call routes to a virtual walkthrough; no explicit rate lock or booking ask on this call. Joanna says 'I'll send you guys a link in a few minutes' and schedules the walkthrough for Wednesday 1:00 PM, confirming the link can be forwarded. No 'Would you like our help with your move?' or rate lock statement before that.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details concern-led, covering addresses, property types, special items (TVs, gym equipment, glass surfaces), packing needs, and box count, creating a solid foundation for the walkthrough estimator.
coaching_note: When the customer raises concerns in step 2, go at least one layer deeper with follow-up silence ('tell me more about that') rather than moving immediately to logistics—this builds the trust that will carry through the walkthrough.
